BiblicalUsage: hălak means to walk. In Daniel 3:25, the text says "walking in the midst of the fire." In Daniel 4:29, the text says "At the end of twelve months he walked in the palace of the kingdom of Babylon."
TheologicalSignificance: For me, hălak is a reminder that obedience is not drudgery; it is trusting that God's way is the good way. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego in the Fiery Furnace; Nebuchadnezzar's Humbling
